subject: English
passage: One challenge when researching whether receiving a major promotion changes an employee's work performance is the problem of ensuring that the study has an appropriate control group. To reveal the effect of promotion, researchers must compare people who receive promotions with people who do not receive promotions but who are otherwise similar to those who were promoted. Since researchers are unable to control which employees companies choose to promote, they therefore ______
prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: struggle to find valid data about the work performance of employees who have not received recent promotions.
choices.B: will find it difficult to identify a group of people who can function as an appropriate control group for their studies.
choices.C: can only conduct valid studies with people who received promotions in the past rather than people who recently received promotions.
choices.D: should select a control group of people who differ from promoted employees in several significant ways.

explanation:
Choice B is the best answer because it presents the conclusion that most logically follows from the text's discussion of the challenge researchers face when studying the effects of promotion on work performance. The text explains that it's hard for researchers to test for the effects that promotion has on employees because finding people to serve as a control group is difficult. The text indicates that a control group needs to be made up of people who share characteristics of the group being tested but don't have the variable being tested (in this case, receiving a promotion). Because researchers aren't able to influence which employees companies promote, they're also unable to determine who would serve as an appropriately similar member of a control group. Thus, it logically follows that researchers will find it difficult to identify a group of people who can function as an appropriate control group for their studies.

Why A is incorrect:

Choice A is incorrect because the text focuses on the struggle to put together a control group for experiments; it doesn't suggest that finding information about employees' performance is difficult.
